transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t really stop worrying. It’s a lot of things at once—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house I keep not finishing. I keep feeling like I’m failing as a husband and a dad.
Do you find that your worrying is excessive and hard to control, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

Yeah… I think so. I’ll try to tell myself to just focus on the code in front of me, or breathe through a workout, but it doesn’t really stop. One thing turns into another, and suddenly I’m way ahead in my head—like a bad review means losing my job, and then my family’s worse off because of me.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, trouble sleeping, or muscle tension, that seem to go along with your worrying?

Yeah… mostly tension, I guess. I feel wound up almost all day. My shoulders are always kind of locked, like I’m bracing for something. And I catch myself pacing between meetings, or tapping pieces at chess club because sitting still just feels… hard.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
I don’t know… not really most of the day every day. I’ve felt pretty worn down, but I wouldn’t say hopeless exactly.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or like you don’t have much energy lately?
I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve been tired, but it’s hard to tell if it’s unusual or just… normal life stuff. I haven’t really tracked it.
Have you found yourself getting more irritable lately, even over small things?
Maybe a little, but… I’m not sure it’s more than usual. I haven’t really been keeping track of that.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these worries and physical symptoms been going on for more than a few months, or did they start more recently in response to a specific stressor?
It’s been… probably around nine months. It started when the cloud migration at work really ramped up, and around the same time things at home started getting tense more regularly.
Do you feel like your anxiety and tension have become a constant part of your daily life, even when things are going okay, or does it seem to come and go depending on the situation?

It feels pretty constant, yeah. Even when nothing is actively going wrong, my mind just keeps jumping between everything—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house I haven’t finished. It’s like I’m always worried I’m dropping the ball somehow.
Have these feelings of worry and tension made it hard for you to function in your job, your relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Yeah… it has. At work my manager’s started writing down things I missed, like architectural details I should’ve caught.

And at home… I’m not really finishing things I start, and I’m distracted a lot. That’s been making the arguments worse.
Do you feel that your level of worry and tension is out of proportion to the actual impact of the problems you’re facing, like feeling like a small issue at work could completely derail your life?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like I can’t stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, work, bills, the house stuff I keep not finishing. It all turns into this feeling that I’m just… failing as a husband and father.

Can you describe how your anxiety felt when the stress at work first started—did it feel like a normal reaction to a tough situation, or was it more intense and difficult to manage from the beginning?

It was more than just normal stress, I think. Even early on, I’d try to just focus on the code in front of me, but my mind would jump ahead—like one issue meant a bad review, and then somehow that meant losing my job and hurting my family. It was hard to pull it back.
Have you noticed that your anxiety and tension are present even in situations where there isn’t an obvious stressor, like when you’re relaxing at home or doing something you enjoy?

Yeah… even when nothing’s really happening. I’ll be at home or between meetings and I still feel wound tight, like my shoulders are locked up and I’m bracing for something. Sometimes I just pace or tap on pieces at chess club because sitting still feels… hard.
Has your anxiety continued even after the cloud migration at work was completed or mostly resolved?
Yeah. It didn’t really go away after that. It’s been… about nine months now, since the migration got intense and things at home started turning into arguments more often.
Do you feel that your anxiety continues even when the actual stressors, like work or home issues, are temporarily resolved or less intense?

Yeah… it does. Even when work quiets down or things at home aren’t actively bad, my head just moves to the next thing. My marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, stuff around the house I haven’t finished… it all kind of piles up. I keep thinking I’m failing as a husband and a father.

Even before the cloud migration and home issues started causing arguments, did you have times when you felt this same level of worry or tension, or has it mostly been tied to these specific stressors?
Mostly it’s been tied to those things. I mean… it really started getting like this about nine months ago, when the cloud migration ramped up and the arguments at home became more regular.
